newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Technology stocks active.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Technology stocks active.

text.p: Options on several technology stocks, including Intel Corp and International Business Machines Corp, were active in morning trading.
On the American Stock Exchange, several longer-dated Intel options were active, continuing a trend started on Friday, when investors were seen moving out of the September contracts.
The Intel January 1997 80 call traded more than 2,400 contracts, the January 1997 60 and 62-1/2 traded 1,000 and 1,100 respectively and the October 85 call traded nearly 900 contracts.
Traders said most of the January 1997 Intel call activity was from spreads.
Intel shares were at their session high, up 1-1/8 at 82-3/8, at 1135 CDT (1635 GMT).
For IBM, the September 115 and 120 calls were active, as were the January 1997 110 call and the October 100 put.
IBM shares were up 1-1/2 at 117, just off their 117-3/8 intraday peak.
Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said investors in the September calls may have been playing the bounce in the stock.
On Tuesday, the computer giant is scheduled to unveil its much-anticipated third generation of its low-cost mainframes.
The company is also scheduled to announce an Internet banking alliance with major U.S. banks later on Monday.
In other activity, three long-term options, or LEAPS, on AT&T Corp were heavily traded in what Schwartz said could be a LEAP married put.
The January 1998 55 call and the January 1998 55 and 60 put each traded about 1,000 contracts.
"They could be buying the stock and the in-the-money puts as a hedged position," Schwartz said. AT&T shares were up 3/4 at 53-1/2.
Schwartz explained that if an investor bought the stock and the LEAPS puts at the same time, the risk on the January 55 puts would be $1.02 while the January 60 puts would create a credit of $0.85.
He added that investors could still be using the LEAPS as a way to play AT&T's spinoff of its Lucent Technologies Inc, scheduled for the end of this month.
"It's a sophisticated way of using LEAPS in conjunction with a spinoff that will result in adjusted options and have minimal risk over the next 495 days," he said.
There are 495 days remaining until the January 1998 LEAPS expire.
